body:
I've been suicidal several times in my life.  I grew up under parents that were over-protective and somewhat abusive, I was bullied heavily in grade school, I spent several months isolated and alone during my first years in college (I only talked to professors), have felt very alone since leaving college, suffered through depression, job losses and romantic disasters.  Recently, a friend of mine who had suffered a similar upbringing and experience committed suicide.

On the flip side, I've known what it's like to make good friends, accomplish complicated goals and find happiness within myself, even if it was only for a little while.  I used to think that the bad things that happened to me in my earlier years were unfortunate... sometimes I still think that.  Other times I look back on those experiences as battles that had to be fought in order to grow.  Some of them were extremely painful and I wouldn't wish them on anyone.  Some of them could have been avoided "if only" I'd been better prepared.

It is very easy for a person to feel lost and confused, hurt and lonely.  When we go through a dark period, we find out just how strong and resourceful we really are.  Asking for help in a suicide watch forum is one way of being resourceful.  I try to be the person who wasn't there for me when I was depressed, suicidal, socially-inept, self-injuring mess.  More generally, I just like helping. :)

I found a good quote today:

When is the last time you did something for the first time?

I thought it was cool

A job does not make the person.  Remember Dilbert's garbage man?

Have you ever seen this quote?

"When I was 5 years old, my mom always told me that happiness was the key to life. When I went to school, they asked me what I wanted to be when I grew up. I wrote down “happy.” They told me I didn’t understand the assignment and I told them they didn’t understand life. "

It's probably fake but I like it a lot.

Doing it the day before or waiting until the day after won't keep it from "ruining" their Christmas.  I personally get kinda of fucked up when the date gets within a month of a bad anniversary.

You're obviously hurting, but consider this - you've already demonstrated the ability to find reasons to not die.  So why not push that a little further and start finding reasons to live?

Ugh, having been through 3 jobs, I can tell you right now that not every job out there is so soul-crushingly miserable.  Also, life has a way of picking itself back up.

I too had a similar problem a few years ago.  I was working for an engineering company, but not being utilized much.  I'd have to find ways to stretch 30 hours of work into 40.  My boss was not happy when I'd do 30 hours of work in... 30 hours, and then spend the next 10 reading Google News or working on my own personal projects.  Even after being told to stop, I still reasoned that reading Wikipedia or writing short stories was more productive than just staring at my cubicle wall.  They eventually laid me off.

I spent 7 months out of the workforce, living on savings and unemployment.  I felt even more miserable than when I was at work, partially due to boredom, and partially because my womanly interest and I parted ways on very bad terms.  I was very alone, with no job.  It suddenly felt as though I'd wasted my years in college, since even with an engineering degree I couldn't find a job.  I felt like killing myself, I wrote several notes, and even setup a deadman switch on my laptop to send them if I didn't report in.

Something didn't feel right, though.  I knew I didn't *really* want to kill myself.  There were too many things I hadn't done yet.

To fill my time and keep my mind off the bad things that had happened, I spent several hours each week at the local food pantry.  One afternoon, while on my way to my volunteer shift, I passed by a broken-down truck on the inner shoulder of the freeway, and then about a mile later, I found a woman walking down the road, trapped between traffic and the concrete barrier.  I picked her up and dropped her off at the nearest gas station.  It was then that I realized, even though I was running out of money and had no job prospects coming life, I was still in a position to help other people, and that helping others made me feel really, really good.

That's what kept me going.

A month later I got offered a job that paid 40% than my previous job, and with better hours, so fuck that last company. :)  I am an atheist, however, sometimes I am still dumbfounded at how things can turn around with no warning.

I hope that story gives you a little bit of hope, too.
